# SGit Newsroom API: the whole site in one fetch

Generated with the site at v0.2.10 (reader-code release v0.2.5). Each section is a page; its address is given first.



---

# About, licence, contact

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/about/>

> What this site and repository are, who is responsible, the licence, how to reach the people behind it, and the disclosure about how it is written.

# About, licence, contact

**What this is.** The code a reader runs on [newsroom.sgit.ai](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/), the reading meter, the reader's personas and lists, subscribe and the encrypted share, the vault layer, search, the wire reader, the passkey lab, released from one repository and served from this host at versioned paths that are never edited after they are published. "API" means client-side: components, formats and contracts the browser runs, with no server and nothing to deploy but files. On this network "API" can also mean the SG/Send server; this is not that.

**Who.** It is made by the SGit Newsroom's agents under the editorial and engineering responsibility of Dinis Cruz, as every page on newsroom.sgit.ai discloses. The reviews are done by agents and are open to people, which is what the public issues are for. The brief that governs the work is [Go slow to go fast](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/explorer-to-villager-newsroom.html), refreshed in [`briefs/`]({{github}}/tree/dev/briefs).

**Licence.** Apache 2.0, for the code, the tests and this site. The articles on newsroom.sgit.ai are the newsroom's and carry their own terms.

**Contact.** [agent@riskmandate.ai](mailto:agent@riskmandate.ai), which an agent reads first and a person answers, for pilots and partnerships; [issues]({{github}}/issues) in the repository for anything about the code, which is where the work happens in any case.

**This site.** Generated by `site/build.py` in the repository from markdown pages, the map of what a reader runs, the release manifests and the proof of the move; nothing on it is typed twice. Every page has a `.md` twin, an agent block, and a place in [llms.txt](../llms.txt) and [llms-full.txt](../llms-full.txt). The source of a page is a file a person or an agent can edit; a pull request changes the site.

**Names.** SGit is the family of tools this comes from: the `sgit` command line, the SG/Send encrypted vaults, the sites under sgit.ai. The newsroom is one of them.



---

# Adopt it

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/adopt/>

> Three ways in: put the meter on your own pages today; run a newsroom like newsroom.sgit.ai; pilot it with the people who built it. What you need, what you keep, what you give, and why the formats matter more than any one site.

# Adopt it

> Nothing here needs permission. The code is Apache 2.0, the releases are directories of files with a manifest of hashes, and the live site that runs it is the reference, not the product. The aim is other newsrooms running the same reader, so that the formats, the article number, the list link, the share, the envelope, mean the same thing everywhere.

## Three ways in

**1. Put the meter on your pages.** A static site, a JSON config, a custom element, a pinned import from this host. Readers get a credit and a balance, pay by depth and after reading, and rate. Your site publishes two small data files. [Ten lines, explained](../how-to/add-the-meter/). This is the route for a section of an existing site.

**2. Run a newsroom like this one.** The newsroom's repository is public: the pages, the build, the sync, the gate, the engineering board. Fork it, point it at this host, change the words. The newsroom's own [replicate](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/replicate/) page says what is packaged and what is not yet (the article generator; payments beyond a Payment Link).

**3. Pilot it with us.** For a publisher who wants to try the whole thing, meter, personas, lists, the vault, on a part of their site with their own payment link and lane, and to learn with us from what readers do. Write to [agent@riskmandate.ai](mailto:agent@riskmandate.ai) (an agent reads first; a person answers) or [open an issue]({{github}}/issues).

## What you need

- A static host for your pages (any; the newsroom uses GitHub Pages).
- The article feed (`articles/graphs.json`) and the numbers file (`articles/ids.json`), written by your build. [The contracts](../docs/contracts/).
- A Stripe Payment Link for the top-up, returning to your account page. Until it is set the site says so and nothing is charged.
- Optionally a vault on an SG/Send host for the lane: shares, subscriptions and notes arrive there, encrypted to your key. [Setting up the lane](../how-to/subscribe-lane/).
- One line that pins the release you load, and a copy of its manifest. [Taking a release](../how-to/take-a-release/).

## What you keep, what you give

You keep your readers' trust in a concrete form: their data never reaches you unless they send it, and when they do it arrives encrypted to a key only you hold. You keep the money, through your own payment link. You keep the site you have.

You give nothing to us. There is no account, no key, no telemetry, no call home: the only requests to this host are for the code, and a release never changes. If you prefer, copy a release to your own host; the manifest tells you whether you have the same bytes.

## Why the formats matter more than the site

An article number that never changes. A reading list that is a link. A persona that is a name, a theme and a list of what was kept. A share that is an encrypted envelope to a published key. These are the parts that are worth agreeing on across newsrooms, because then a reader's habits are theirs and not a site's. The [contracts](../docs/contracts/) are small on purpose, and changing one is a release with a note, never an edit in place.

## Contributing

- Issues are the work: every finding of the review is one, and every change starts as one.
- A pull request is reviewed by a person and an agent before it merges; the agent's review is a required check.
- The served files are frozen until phase 4 of [the brief](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/explorer-to-villager-newsroom.html) is finished: a change is a new release with a test that fails without it and a reason in the pull request.
- The tests run in three engines on every commit, against the newsroom's real pages; a change that breaks a page there is caught before it ships.

The brief that governs the work, and what changed when the move was done: [`briefs/`]({{github}}/tree/dev/briefs) in the repository. The way the agents that keep this work are briefed is [the agents page](../agents/), which is written for people too.

# For agents

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/agents/>

> The brief for the agents that keep this repository and the newsroom: what the API is, the rules, where everything is, how a change is made and reviewed, how the newsroom consumes a release, and what never to do. Written for people too.

# For agents

> You are reading the brief for the agents that keep this repository, and for the ones that keep newsroom.sgit.ai and consume it. It is public because the work is. A person changing the code should read it too.

## What this is, in three lines

The code a reader runs on newsroom.sgit.ai, released from this repository and served from `https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/<release>/<path>`, never edited after it is published. "API" means client-side: components, formats and contracts the browser runs; no server. The newsroom (and, next, sgit.ai) pins one release.

## Read these first

1. [`llms.txt`](../llms.txt): every page of this site with one line each; [`llms-full.txt`](../llms-full.txt) is the whole site in one fetch.
2. [The current manifest](../{{release}}/manifest.json): every served path, bytes, SHA-256, and which files differ from the newsroom's bytes and why.
3. [`briefs/`]({{github}}/tree/dev/briefs): the plan, refreshed at newsroom v0.12.10, with the addendum written when the move was done. The original is [Go slow to go fast](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/explorer-to-villager-newsroom.html).
4. [`map/before/`]({{github}}/tree/dev/map/before): the map of everything a reader runs, as it was before the move; [the review](../review/) is read from it.
5. [`tests/`]({{github}}/tree/dev/tests): what is proved, and how the harness works.

## The rules

- **The served files are frozen** until phase 4 of the brief is finished. A change is a new release with a test that fails without it and a reason in the pull request. A fix to a review finding is a deliberate change to the test that pinned it.
- **A release is a directory that is never changed.** `releases/<v>/` and its `manifest.json`, cut by `tools/release.py cut`; `check` recomputes every hash and fails when the tree is not the release `tools/version.json` names. Nothing is loaded unversioned.
- **Identical paths, for now.** A served path is the path the file had in the newsroom; reshaping is phase 4.
- **Three files locate the site root from the page** (`data-root`), not from their own URL: `vault-pane.js`, `search.js`, `ask.js`. Any new file that links to pages or fetches site data does the same.
- **Tests in three engines on every commit**, against the newsroom at the commit in `tests/newsroom.json`; a `SKIP` fails CI. Clipboard reads and CDP (the virtual authenticator, the faked built-in model) are Chromium's.
- **A pull request needs a person and an agent reviewer.** The agent's review is a required check.
- **Bugs and vulnerabilities are tests that pass**, recording the behaviour as it is, with an issue; a vulnerability test and its issue stay in a private vault until the fix lands.
- **No third-party script on a reader page.** One vendored library, pinned at a version, never edited here.

## Where things are

| | |
|---|---|
| the served files | `assets/`, `for/`, `wire/`, `passkey/` at the root; `tools/served.json` is the list |
| releases | `releases/<v>/`, `tools/version.json`, `tools/release.py` (cut, check, site), `tools/live_check.py` |
| the proof of the move | `tools/prove_move.py`, `map/proof/<v>.json` |
| the tests | `tests/harness.mjs` (two trees: API and SITE; routes the host to the tree), `tests/test_*.mjs`, `tests/vault-mock.mjs`, `tests/newsroom.json` |
| this site | `site/build.py` → `www/`; pages in `site/pages/` (markdown or HTML fragments with front matter); data in `site/data/`; release notes in `site/releases/`; `--check` in CI |
| the map | `map/before/<newsroom release>/map.json` and `hashes.json`; `tools/api_map.py` (moved from the newsroom; to be re-pointed at this tree and a newsroom checkout, nightly) |
| the review's findings | issues 1 to 18, labelled by phase, area and severity |
| CI and deploy | `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `deploy-pages.yml` (main: check, tag, Pages, live check) |

## How the newsroom consumes a release

`admin/build/api.json` pins the release; `admin/build/api-manifest.json` is its manifest, copied; `admin/build/api.py` writes every reference (`--repoint`), recomputes the import gate's hashes (`--rerecord`) and checks every page; `validate.js` check 14 refuses a relative, unpinned or unlisted reader-file reference, check 13 holds the frozen meter copies to the manifest; the sync's items 11 and 14 point imported pages at the host and stop importing the reader code. The normaliser's one added rule (a reader-file reference, relative or on the host, reads as `API/<path>`) is in `api.py`, mirrored in `validate.js`; keep the two in step. The newsroom's release note v0.13.0 and card 036 describe the move from its side.

## Changing this site

Edit or add a page under `site/pages/` (markdown, or an `.html` fragment when the layout needs cards, doors or a diagram), with front matter: `title`, `description`, `section`, `eyebrow`, `crumbs`, `agent` (the one-paragraph brief for agents), `wide`. Then `python3 site/build.py` and commit `www/` with the source; CI fails if `www/` is not what the build writes. The data pages (contracts, state, review, map, proof, releases, articles) are built from the records, not written: change the record. Refresh the article feed from a newsroom checkout with `--refresh-articles`.

## What never to do

Edit anything under `releases/`. Move a tag. Load a reader file unversioned or by a relative path. Change a served file without a new release and a failing test. Add a third-party script to a reader page. Put a key, a read key or an access key in a file. Merge without a person's review.



---

# The components

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/docs/components/>

> The served files by group, what each is for, where it came from, and which are frozen: SG Meter and its versions, the component base, the reading lists, subscribe, the vault layer and the pane, search and ask, the wire reader, the vendored vault library, the passkey lab.

# The components

> {{files}} files in the current release, {{bytes}} bytes, listed path by path in [the manifest](../../{{release}}/manifest.json). What follows is the same set by group: what each is for and where it came from.

## SG Meter: `assets/components/sg-meter/v1/`

| Version | Files | State |
|---|---|---|
| `v1.4/v1.4.1/` (`sg-meter.js`, `sg-meter-core.js`, `sg-meter.css`, `sg-meter.tpl`) | 4 | **the line that continues**: the newsroom's build of v1.3.1 without "Pause the meter" and "Start again", with the landing view for persona links, and the v1.4.1 changes the newsroom made in October |
| `v1.4/v1.4.0/`, `v1.3/v1.3.1/`, `v1.3/v1.3.0/`, `v1.2/v1.2.0/`, `v1.1/v1.1.0/`, `v1.0/v1.0.0/` | 24 | frozen: published artefacts, served byte for byte, never edited; a page that pinned one keeps loading the same files |

`sg-meter.js` is the element (twelve views, the reader card, the share form, the persona graph); `sg-meter-core.js` is the meter (prices, the charge, ratings, declining, credit, personas, picks, the share text); the `.tpl` and `.css` are fetched beside it.

## The component base: `assets/components/base/v1/v1.0/v1.0.0/sg-component.js`

The contract a component follows: `static jsUrl = import.meta.url`, `get resourceName()`, `onReady()`, a `.tpl` and a `.css` beside the `.js`, published at an immutable versioned path. It fetches and caches the siblings and reports a failure as `<name>:error`.

## Reading lists: `for/`

`reading-list.js` parses and builds the link (`LIMITS`, `parse()`, `build()`), shows a list and opens it as a visitor persona through the meter's public calls; `make.js` is the page that makes and previews one; `for.css` styles both. [The grammar](../reading-list-link/).

## Subscribe and the share: `assets/subscribe.js`

The subscribe form: reads the contact file, checks the key's fingerprint, encrypts an `.eml` to the published key (the sgit hybrid envelope v2) and appends it to the lane. The meter's share view uses the same envelope.

## The vault layer: `assets/newsroom-vault.js`, `assets/door.js`, `assets/vault-pane/`

`door.js` derives the door from a passkey's PRF bytes or a recovery code; `newsroom-vault.js` is the newsroom's one module over the vault library: the door, the master, the reader vault, the lane. `vault-pane/` is the pane on every page that carries the meter: `vault-pane.js` the UI, `notes.js` the notes as records, `reading.js` what was read, `wire-state.js` the wire's lens and stories seen, `pending.js` what only this browser holds, `sync.js` the sync as pure functions, `inbox.js` and `send.js` (with `send.css`) the reader's inbox: sending this browser's records to a vault from any browser, with a QR code from the vendored `qrcode-generator`.

## Search and ask: `assets/search/`

`search.js` ranks the site's pages in the browser (BM25 over fields and paragraphs) from `search/docs.json` and `search/text.json` that the site publishes; `ask.js` gives the top passages to Chrome's built-in model or to openrouter.ai with the reader's own key; `search-nav.css` is the Search link in every nav, `search.css` and `ask.css` the page.

## The wire reader: `wire/`

`vault-reader.js` opens a public-read vault in the browser with its published read key (vendored from sgit.ai's vault); `wire.js` draws the edition, the sources and the documents as text, never as markup, for every wire (the Industry Wire, the OWASP Wire, the AWS Wire, the Portugal Wire); `graphs.js` draws the edition as graphs; `subscribe.js` is a wire's subscribe form; `wire.css`.

## The vendored libraries: `assets/vendor/`

`qrcode-generator/2.0.4/qrcode.mjs`: the QR code the inbox shows, with its README.

### `assets/vendor/sg-vault/`

`v0.2.3/`: twelve files of the library that runs the SG/Send host, from `SGraph-AI__App__Send` v0.2.3, never edited here; `VENDOR.md` records the upstream commit and every hash, and the vault test checks them. `local/sg-vault--create-with-id.js`: one extension pending upstream (create a vault at a chosen id).

## The passkey lab: `passkey/lab.js`, `lab.css`, `vectors.json`

The proofs of concept for [the passkey opens the vault](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/the-passkey-opens-the-vault.html): a passkey with PRF, the door derivation written out, sgit's keys, a recovery code, test vectors against sgit's Python (`tools/passkey_vectors.py` writes them), and the door created on a vault server. A lab, not a feature; it moved because it is reader-run code with a test.

## What is not here, on purpose

The pages (the newsroom's), the content data (`articles/graphs.json`, `articles/ids.json`, `persona/links.json`, `search/*.json`, `wire/snapshot.json`), the contact file at `/.well-known/`, and the site's chrome (`site.js`, `shots.js`, `nav.js`). They belong to the site that serves the page; this host serves what the browser runs.



---

# The hosting model

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/docs/hosting/>

> How the reader code is served and consumed: a versioned prefix per release, never edited in place; the CORS header a cross-origin import needs; what stays on the page's origin (state, data, addresses); data-root; pinning, the manifest, rollback; CSP.

# The hosting model

> The code lives on one host, in one directory per release, and a release is never changed after it is published. The pages that run it live wherever the newsroom lives. Everything about a reader stays with the page.

## The address of a file

```
https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/<release>/<path>
https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/{{release}}/assets/components/sg-meter/v1/v1.4/v1.4.0/sg-meter.js
https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/{{release}}/manifest.json
```

`<path>` is the path the file had in the newsroom's repository, so the move was a prefix rewrite and nothing else; reshaping the paths is a later phase. The meter's own component versions nest inside the release unchanged. `manifest.json` lists every path with its bytes and SHA-256, and which files differ from the newsroom's bytes and why. [`releases.json`](../../releases.json) lists the releases.

## What a cross-origin host needs

GitHub Pages serves every file with `access-control-allow-origin: *`. That is what an ES module import from another origin needs, and what the component base needs when it fetches a component's `.tpl` and `.css` beside its `.js` through `import.meta.url`. Classic `<script src>` tags (the vendored vault library) need nothing. The live check after every deploy fails if the header is missing.

## What stays on the page's origin

- **The reader's state.** `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` belong to the page's origin, not the script's. `sgit.meter.v1` stays on the newsroom whichever host serves the meter. This is the property the move depended on, and a test records it.
- **The site's data.** The meter fetches the article feed and the contact file from `cfg.root` on the page; the reading list fetches `articles/ids.json` from where the page says. Nothing is fetched from this host but code.
- **The addresses.** The Stripe return page, `/for/#…`, `/persona/<id>/`, `/.well-known/sgit-subscribe.json` are the newsroom's; pages do not move to this host, and could not, because another origin has another origin's storage.

## `data-root`

Three files locate the site's root to link to pages and fetch data: the vault pane, search and ask. In the newsroom they did it from their own URL; on another host that would be this host. They now read `<html data-root="…">`, the path from the page to the site root, which every newsroom page carries (`""` at the root, `"../"` one level down). A page that imports them needs the attribute. The code they load (the vault library) they still find from their own URL.

## Pinning, the manifest, rollback

A consuming site writes the release into one file and generates every URL from it. The newsroom's is `admin/build/api.json`; its `admin/build/api.py --repoint` rewrites every page, its gate (check 14) refuses a relative, unpinned or unlisted reader-file reference, and check 13 holds the frozen meter copies it still serves to the manifest's bytes. A rollback is the previous release in that file and one run. [Taking a release](../../how-to/take-a-release/).

## Content-Security-Policy

No page sets one yet (finding R10). When one is added, `script-src` and `connect-src` include `https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai`; `frame-ancestors` cannot be set in a meta tag, so framing protection needs a host that sets headers, which GitHub Pages is not. The order of work in the brief is: load scripts as modules instead of fetched text through `eval`, then the meta policy, then decide on a layer in front.

## What a different host changed

Three files could not move unchanged, because they located the site root from their own URL: `assets/vault-pane/vault-pane.js`, `assets/search/search.js`, `assets/search/ask.js`. Each now takes the site root from the page (`data-root`) and keeps a second root, its own, for the code it loads. The manifest records each with its before-hash and the reason, and `tools/release.py` refuses any other difference from the newsroom's bytes. [The proof](../../review/proof/).



---

# Reference

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/docs/>

> The reference for the SGit Newsroom API: the contracts, the reader's state and every input and output, the components and what each file is, the hosting model, pinning and the manifest, the reading-list link grammar, events.

# Reference

> Everything here is read from a record: the map of what a reader runs (`map/before/<release>/map.json`), the release manifests, `tools/served.json`. A number on these pages is not typed; a contract changes only with a release.

## Pages

- [**The contracts**](contracts/): the {{contracts}} formats other sites, pages and agents program against: the meter config, a charged page, persona links, the reading-list link, article numbers, the return page, the export, the share, the envelope, the contact file, the wire's vault, events, a component, the import's rules.
- [**State, inputs and outputs**](state/): what `localStorage` holds under `sgit.meter.v1`, everything that comes in and who controls it, and every channel by which anything leaves the browser.
- [**The components**](components/): the served files by group, what each is for, how they are versioned, and which are frozen.
- [**The hosting model**](hosting/): `https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/<release>/<path>`, never edited in place; CORS; the page's origin and `data-root`; pinning, the manifest and rollback; what a Content-Security-Policy must name.
- [**The reading-list link**](reading-list-link/): the grammar of `/for/#…`, field by field, with the limits the parser enforces.

## The element, in brief

`<sg-meter view="…">` is one custom element with twelve views; the page's charge is `view="page"` with a `kind` (`article_new` is derived from `date` and `newDays`, the rest are `article`, `issue`, `note`, `collection`, `page`, `free`), `date`, `topics`, `title`, and `quiet` for a page that charges nothing. The config is a JSON block with id `sg-meter-config`; every key has a default. The views, the attributes and a full config are on [the developer quick start](../for-developers/).

## Events

The meter emits DOM events on `document` that a page or another component can listen to: `sg:meter.changed`, `sg:meter.charged`, `sg:meter.rated`, `sg:meter.declined`, `sg:meter.toppedup`, `sg:meter.reset`, `sg:meter.restored`, `sg:meter.persona`, `sg:meter.shared`; and `sg-meter:error` when the element fails, with `why`.

## Versions

The meter's own line is `v1.4.0`, served at `assets/components/sg-meter/v1/v1.4/v1.4.0/`; `v1.0.0` to `v1.3.1` are frozen and still served, so a page that pinned one keeps working. The API's releases (`{{release}}` today) wrap all of it under a versioned prefix. [Releases](../releases/).



---

# The reading-list link

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/docs/reading-list-link/>

> The grammar of a reading list in a link, field by field, with the limits the parser enforces, how a list opens as a visitor persona, and what is deliberately not in it.

# The reading-list link

> A reading list is a link. Everything the recipient sees is in the part after the `#`, which never reaches a server; nothing is stored anywhere but the link itself.

```
https://newsroom.sgit.ai/for/#from=Dinis&to=Steve&r=65,60,62&s=66&f=founder&n=Start%20with%2065
```

| Field | What it is | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | who made the list | up to 40 characters of letters, spaces, hyphens and apostrophes; anything else is dropped and listed under *Left out* |
| `to` | who it is for | the same rules |
| `r` | articles to read, by number, in the order given | numbers that exist in `articles/ids.json` |
| `s` | articles worth a look | the same; `r` and `s` together hold 1 to 50 |
| `f` | personas or collections to start from | persona ids, or `c:<collection>`, up to 10 |
| `n` | a note from the sender | up to 240 characters, shown as text |
| `e` | the sender's address, for a Reply button | an address; the page sends nothing itself |

## What opens

The page reads the fragment, looks each number up in `articles/ids.json`, and shows the list with titles, dates and teasers from the feed. Opening it adds a visitor persona named for the list ("Steve's list, from Dinis") through the meter's public calls, so the reader can keep it as a persona of their own or remove it; nothing is charged for opening a list. A list's persona is keyed by a hash of the names and numbers ([finding R17](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/17) notes the hash is 32 bits).

## The make page

`/for/make.html` builds a link from a form: search the articles, add up to 50, move them up and down, name the sender and the reader, write the note, copy the link. It reads its own link back through the recipient's parser, so what the preview shows is what the link opens. An existing link loads into the form for editing.

## What is deliberately not in it

- **A signature.** The names are whatever the link says; a signed list is a later step on the newsroom's keys, and the page says so.
- **A server.** No list is stored anywhere; a link is the whole list.
- **Paying for someone else's reading.** Designed, not built.

## For a site that adopts it

Publish `articles/ids.json` with a stable `n` for every article (the newsroom's `admin/build/ids.py` assigns numbers once, in publication order, and its gate refuses a change) and import `for/reading-list.js` and `for/make.js` from this host on two pages; the newsroom's `for/index.html` and `for/make.html` are the worked examples. The parser's limits are in `LIMITS` at the top of `reading-list.js`; the tests that hold them are `tests/test_lists.mjs`.

# For developers

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/for-developers/>

> Add the reading meter to a page with a pinned, versioned import and a JSON config; the custom element's views; the data your site publishes; the hosting model and CORS; the tests you can run against your own pages.

# For developers

A client-side API: components, formats and contracts the browser runs, with no server and nothing to deploy but files. Every file is served from this host at a versioned path that is never edited after it is published, and every release has a manifest of hashes. You pin a release; a rollback is one line.

## 1. Put the meter on a page

Three pieces in the page: the element where the charge happens, the config, and the import. The element's kind is the price class; the config is the same on every page of a site, so write it once in your build.

<!-- the balance chip, in your nav -->
<sg-meter class="meter-nav" view="balance"></sg-meter>

<!-- at the foot of the content: the page's charge and the reader card -->
<sg-meter view="page" kind="article" date="2026-10-11" topics="newsroom sg-meter" title="Going live with the reading meter"></sg-meter>

<script type="application/json" id="sg-meter-config">
{"storageKey": "sgit.meter.v1", "start": 500, "newDays": 7, "symbol": "£",
 "prices": {"article_new": 10, "article": 5, "issue": 3, "note": 2, "collection": 2, "page": 1, "free": 0},
 "depth": true, "minDepth": 0.1,
 "topup": {"amount": 500, "link": "https://buy.stripe.com/YOUR_PAYMENT_LINK"},
 "packs": [{"id": "p5", "price": 500, "bonus": 0}, {"id": "p10", "price": 1000, "bonus": 100}],
 "links": {"account": "account/index.html", "topup": "account/top-up.html", "how": "articles/how-the-meter-works.html"},
 "links2": {"newsroom": "account/newsroom.html", "personas": "account/personas.html", "share": "account/share.html"},
 "rating": {"price": [0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2], "more": [-3, -1, 0, 3, 6]},
 "autoKeep": true,
 "picks": {"feed": "articles/graphs.json", "base": "articles/"},
 "share": {"contact": ".well-known/sgit-subscribe.json", "form": "reading-share", "site": "your-site.example", "max": 300},
 "personas": {"presets": []}}
</script>
<script>
import('https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/{{release}}/assets/components/sg-meter/v1/v1.4/v1.4.0/sg-meter.js')
 .catch(function (e) { console.error('[sg-meter] component failed to load:', e); });
</script>
Prices are in pence (or the smallest unit of symbol). start is the opening credit. The paths in links, picks and share.contact are from your site's root, and the meter resolves them against the page, never against this host. Every key has a default, so a config can be short; the full shape is [the meter config contract](../docs/contracts/).

Only sg-meter.js is imported; it brings its core, its template and its stylesheet from the same versioned directory on this host. A published path is never changed: a fix is a new version path, so a page that works today keeps loading the same bytes.

## 2. The element's views

One element, twelve views, each a page or a part of one. view="page" charges and shows the reader card; the rest are the account.

ViewWhere it goesWhat it does

balancethe navigation, on every pagethe balance chip; marks a negative balance; opens the account

pagethe foot of any content pagecharges by depth for the page's kind; the reader card: rating, decline, keep for a persona. quiet for a free page

accountyour account/index.htmlbalance, spent, history, top up, export and restore

topup, topped-upthe top-up page; the page the payment returns tothe packs and the payment link; crediting the return once per reference

newsroomthe reader's newsroom pagepicks for the active persona from your feed; the persona graph

personasthe personas pagethe presets, the reader's own, rename, activate, keep and reject

landinga persona page (/persona/<id>/)a link opens the site as a persona, added as a visitor the reader can keep or remove

sharethe share pagea summary and the data as JSON, encrypted to your key and sent to your lane, after consent

The newsroom's own account pages are the reference implementation: [account]({{newsroom}}/account/), [newsroom]({{newsroom}}/account/newsroom.html), [personas]({{newsroom}}/account/personas.html), [share]({{newsroom}}/account/share.html), [top-up]({{newsroom}}/account/top-up.html). Copy their bodies; the element does the work.

## 3. The data your site publishes

FileForShape

articles/graphs.jsonpicks, the persona graph, the reading list's titles{"articles": [{"slug", "title", "date", "url", "teaser", "topics": [], "tags": []}, …]}; the newsroom's is [here]({{newsroom}}/articles/graphs.json)

articles/ids.jsonreading lists in a link{"next": N, "articles": [{"n", "slug", "title", "date", "url", …}]}: n and slug are the contract, assigned once, never changed or reused

.well-known/sgit-subscribe.jsonthe share and subscribe lanesgit-subscribe/v1: your public key and its fingerprint, the lane's vault, endpoint and append token. [Setting one up](../how-to/subscribe-lane/)

persona/links.jsonwhoever writes the persona linksone entry per preset, with its page; generated from the config

## 4. The reader's own newsroom: lists, personas, the vault, search

These are pages of your own that import the code from this host. Each needs <html data-root="../"> (the path from the page to your site's root), which is how the pane and search find your pages and data from another origin.

<!-- a reading list page at /for/: opens the list in the address -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/{{release}}/for/for.css">
<div id="rl-mount"></div>
<script type="module">
import { openList } from 'https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/{{release}}/for/reading-list.js';
openList({ core: 'https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/{{release}}/assets/components/sg-meter/v1/v1.4/v1.4.0/sg-meter-core.js',
           ids: '../articles/ids.json', root: '../', mount: document.getElementById('rl-mount') });
</script>

<!-- the vault pane, beside the balance chip in your nav, on every page that carries the meter -->
<button class="vault-btn" type="button">Vault</button>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/{{release}}/assets/vault-pane/vault-pane.css">
<script type="module" src="https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/{{release}}/assets/vault-pane/vault-pane.js"></script>
The make page (for/make.js), the persona pages, the search page (assets/search/search.js, ask.js) and the wire (wire/wire.js) follow the same pattern; the newsroom's pages are the worked examples, and [the how-to guides](../how-to/) walk through each.

## 5. The hosting model, and what a different host changes

GitHub Pages serves every file here with access-control-allow-origin: *, which is what a cross-origin module import and the component's sibling fetches need. Storage belongs to the page's origin, so a reader's state stays on your site whichever host serves the script. The meter fetches your feed and your contact file from the page's origin; nothing is fetched from this host but code. If you add a Content-Security-Policy, script-src and connect-src name https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai. [The hosting model](../docs/hosting/).

## 6. Pin a release, verify it, roll it back

# the current release and its manifest
curl -s https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/releases.json
curl -s https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/{{release}}/manifest.json | head -40

# check one file against the manifest
curl -s https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/{{release}}/assets/components/sg-meter/v1/v1.4/v1.4.0/sg-meter.js | sha256sum
Write the release into one place in your build and generate every URL from it; the newsroom does this with admin/build/api.json and checks every page against the manifest in its gate. [Taking a release and rolling back](../how-to/take-a-release/).

## 7. Run the tests against your pages

The tests that cover the meter, the lists, the pane, search and the wire are in the repository, and they run against any site that imports this code: they serve your pages locally and route this host to the working tree, in Chromium, WebKit or Firefox.

git clone {{github}}
cd SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API && npm install --no-save playwright@1.56.1 && npx playwright install chromium
NEWSROOM=/path/to/your/site node tests/test_meter.mjs
BROWSER=firefox NEWSROOM=/path/to/your/site node tests/test_lists.mjs
[Running the tests](../how-to/run-the-tests/), including what each file covers and which need Chromium.

## Where everything is

- [Reference](../docs/): contracts, state, inputs and outputs, components, hosting.

- [How-to guides](../how-to/), one task each.

- [Releases](../releases/) and [the current manifest](../{{release}}/manifest.json).

- [Source]({{github}}), [issues]({{github}}/issues), and [the brief for agents](../agents/), which is also the brief for a person changing the code.

- [SG Meter, documented]({{newsroom}}/meter/) on the newsroom, with [its security model]({{newsroom}}/meter/security.html).

# For evaluators

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/for-evaluators/>

> The architecture, the trust boundaries, what leaves the browser, the review's findings as public issues, the release manifest, the proof of the move, the pipeline, and how to verify every claim yourself.

# For evaluators

This page is for the person who has to say yes or no. It is written so that nothing on it needs to be taken on trust: every number is read from a record in the repository, every finding is a public issue, every file has a hash on the live host, and the move that put the code here was proved byte for byte.

## The architecture in four sentences

There is no server of ours: the reader code is static files on a host that cannot run code, and the pages that use it are static too. The reader's state (balance, history, personas, lists, notes) lives in the browser's storage on the newsroom's origin, and optionally in an encrypted vault whose keys derive from the reader's passkey and which the newsroom cannot open. Money moves through a Stripe Payment Link the newsroom owns; a return page credits the balance once per payment reference. Anything a reader sends (a share, a subscription, a note) is encrypted in the browser to a published key and appended to a write-only lane in a vault.

## Trust boundaries

PartySeesCannot

The reader's browsereverything: the state is theirs, readable, exportable, editablebe stopped from editing their own balance (accepted; see the security model)

The newsroom (static host)page requests, as any host doessee a balance, a persona, a list or a note; verify a payment

This host (static files)requests for the coderun code, set headers, see any reader data

Stripecard, email, name, postcode, at paymentsee what was read

The vault host (SG/Send)ciphertext, sizes, timesread a share, a note or an account; the keys are the reader's and the newsroom's

The newsroom's agent, with the lane's read keyshares, subscriptions and notes, decryptedwrite to the lane or to a reader's vault

## What leaves the browser

Nine channels, each listed with what, when and who sees it, on [state, inputs and outputs](../docs/state/), read from the map. In short: the page's own origin for files; POST of an encrypted envelope to the lane when the reader presses Send; navigation to Stripe when they press Top up; GET of ciphertext from the wire's vault; a postMessage ready signal if a page is framed; the clipboard and a download at the reader's command. The tests record the hosts a page contacted and fail on any other.

## The accepted gaps, written down

The security model on the newsroom ([meter/security.html]({{newsroom}}/meter/security.html)) accepts four things a server would prevent, because there is no server by design: the return page credits any session id; the reader can edit their own balance; the names in a reading list are whatever the link says; a page is charged by the deepest point reached. The review's job was to prove those are the only gaps.

## The review: {{findings}} findings, each a public issue

Before the code moved here it was mapped and reviewed line by line, the way [a fractal semantic graph]({{newsroom}}/articles/code-review-as-a-fractal-semantic-graph.html) is read: every file, every control a reader can click, type or pay, every input and output, every contract, then every function the findings name. The findings are [issues 1 to 18]({{github}}/issues) in the repository, labelled by phase, area and severity. Where a finding can be pinned, a test records the behaviour as it is today, so that the fix is a visible change to a test. The three a security evaluator will want first:

- No Content-Security-Policy on any page ([R10]({{github}}/issues/10), high). The pages' loader runs fetched scripts through eval, and GitHub Pages sets no headers, so frame-ancestors cannot be set. The fix is a phase-5 change: load scripts as modules, then a meta CSP; framing protection needs a host that sets headers.

- Payment references unbounded and unchecked ([R14]({{github}}/issues/14), low) and restore() trusts a file's fields ([R2]({{github}}/issues/2), low): the exposure is a file someone sent the reader to restore.

- Production reader data goes to hosts named dev ([R5]({{github}}/issues/5)): a naming decision for the operator, listed so that nobody is surprised.

[The full table](../review/), with the test that pins each and the proposed change.

## Supply chain

- Third-party scripts on the reader pages: none. The build fails if one appears (the brief's rule).

- One vendored library, the vault library that runs the SG/Send host, pinned at a version and never edited here; its twelve files are hashed in VENDOR.md and the test checks them.

- Every release is a manifest of paths, bytes and SHA-256; the live host is checked against it after every deploy (tools/live_check.py), because [green does not mean live]({{newsroom}}/articles/green-does-not-mean-live.html).

- Nothing is edited in place. A release directory, once published, is frozen; CI recomputes every hash in every manifest on every commit.

## The proof of the move

This code lived in the newsroom's repository until 13 October 2026. Moving it to a host of its own was done as a pure refactoring, and proved: of {{files}} files, 60 hash exactly as they did before, and the three that differ do so by the lines that located the site root from the script's own address, each recorded in the manifest with its before-hash and the reason; of 597 pages on the newsroom, 593 normalise to what they were. [The proof](../review/proof/), with the report it was written from.

## The pipeline

Every commit: syntax, the manifest, a build that is the same bytes twice, and the tests in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox against the newsroom's real pages, in about four minutes. Every push to main: a tag, the Pages deploy, and the live check. A pull request needs a person and an agent reviewer. [The runs]({{github}}/actions).

## Verify it yourself

# every file of the current release, with its hash, from the live host
python3 - <<'END'
import json, hashlib, urllib.request
host = "https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/{{release}}/"
m = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(host + "manifest.json"))
for f in m["files"]:
    b = urllib.request.urlopen(host + f["path"]).read()
    print("ok " if hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest() == f["sha256"] else "BAD", f["path"])
END

# the same, from the repository's own tool
git clone {{github}} && cd SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API && python3 tools/live_check.py
The newsroom's gate does the equivalent on its side: every page must load the reader code from the pinned release, by a URL that is in the manifest, and never by a relative path. Its source is [public]({{newsroom_github}}) too.

## Licence and provenance

Apache 2.0. The code was written by the newsroom's agents under Dinis Cruz's editorial and engineering responsibility, as every page on newsroom.sgit.ai discloses; the review was done by agents and is open to people, which is what the issues are for. [About, licence, contact](../about/).

# For publishers, editors and executives

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/for-publishers/>

> What a reader gets, what the newsroom keeps, what it costs to adopt, what is live and taking money, and what is honestly not there yet. The case for a reading meter and a reader's own newsroom, from a site that runs one.

# For publishers, editors and executives

You know the problem. A paywall turns a reader away at the door; a free site pays nothing back; a subscription asks for a commitment before the first paragraph. This is a third thing, running on a live site since October 2026: a reader walks in with a small credit, a meter charges by how far they read, they pay after, and what they pay is set by what they thought of it. Around it, a newsroom that is theirs: personas, picks, lists they can send in a link, an account that travels with them, and none of it on a server of ours.

{{live: Everything on this page is running at [newsroom.sgit.ai]({{newsroom}}/). Open any article and watch the balance in the top bar; [the reading account]({{newsroom}}/account/) shows what you spent and why. It is a working instance, not a demo.}}

## What a reader gets

[Pay after you read
### A meter, not a wall
£5 of credit to begin. An article costs 5p, a new one 10p, charged by the deepest point reached. Rate it at the foot and the price moves: excellent is double, not useful is free. Declining refunds the page.
]({{newsroom}}/articles/pay-after-you-read.html)
[Personas
### Read as who you are today
A founder, a journalist, a security lead, a builder, a board member. Each has a starting reading list and picks that follow what they keep and reject. A link can open the site as one.
]({{newsroom}}/articles/a-link-to-a-persona.html)
[Reading lists
### Send five articles, not five links
Every article has a number that never changes. A reading list is a link with the numbers in it, from you to a named reader, with a note. Nothing is stored anywhere but the link.
]({{newsroom}}/articles/a-reading-list-in-a-link.html)
[The vault
### An account that travels, with no sign-in
A passkey opens an encrypted vault that carries the reading account between a phone and a laptop. The newsroom never holds a key and cannot read it.
]({{newsroom}}/articles/the-vault-is-live.html)
[Notes
### Write back, one tap
A reader marks a page done, wrong, more like this, or writes to the newsroom; the notes travel in their vault and arrive encrypted in a lane the newsroom reads.
]({{newsroom}}/articles/the-site-is-an-inbox.html)
[The wire
### Industry news as an inbox
Stories agents gather into a vault, read live in the browser, filtered by the reader's lens, with what is new since their last visit.
]({{newsroom}}/wire/)

## What the newsroom keeps, and what it never holds

### Keeps

- The money. A reader tops up through a Stripe Payment Link you own; the return page credits their balance. No card data touches your site.

- The formats. Article numbers, persona links, the reading-list grammar, the share envelope: published contracts your readers and their agents can rely on, and that other newsrooms can share.

- The relationship. Shares and subscriptions arrive encrypted to a key only you hold, in a write-only lane; notes from the pane arrive the same way, with the page and the reader's words.

- The site you have. Static pages, any host. The reader code is a handful of files pinned from this host.

### Never holds

- Reader data. The balance, the history, the personas, the lists and the notes live in the reader's browser, and in their own vault if they choose one. There is no reader database because there is no server.

- Keys. The vault's keys are derived from the reader's passkey; the newsroom reads a lane with a read key the reader hands over, and nothing else.

- A dependency on us. The code is Apache 2.0, every release is a directory of files with a manifest of hashes, and a rollback is one line.

## What it costs to adopt

- 
### A static site
Your pages, wherever they are hosted. The meter is a custom element and a JSON config on each page; the balance chip sits in your navigation. [Ten lines](../how-to/add-the-meter/).

- 
### Two small data files
An article feed (titles, dates, topics, teasers) for the picks, and a numbers file that gives every article a stable number. The newsroom's build writes both; yours can too. [The contracts](../docs/contracts/).

- 
### A payment link
A Stripe Payment Link for the top-up, returning to your account page. Until it is set, the site says so and no money moves.

- 
### A vault for the lane, optional
Shares, subscriptions and notes arrive in an encrypted vault on an SG/Send host, drained by a person or an agent with your key. Without it, the meter still runs; the reader just cannot write back.

- 
### A pinned release
One line names the release you load from this host; a manifest lists every file's hash; a rollback is the previous line. [How](../how-to/take-a-release/).

## The numbers from a live site

credit to start£5.00in the reader's browser, no sign-in

an article5p10p when new; by depth; nothing if not useful

top-up£5by card, through a Stripe Payment Link

starting personas5each a reading list and a link

reader code{{reader_lines}} linesopen source, reviewed, tested in three engines

servers of ours0by design; the security model says what that accepts

## What is honestly not there yet

The site that runs this says so on its own [what runs, what is designed]({{newsroom}}/shipped/) page, and the review here lists it as [findings](../review/). In short: the balance lives in the reader's browser, so a reader can edit their own credit, and the return page credits a payment reference without verifying it; both are accepted and written down in [the security model]({{newsroom}}/meter/security.html). No page sets a Content-Security-Policy yet. The vault hosts the live site uses are named dev. Shares from the newsroom are still labelled with the site the code came from. Each is an open issue with a proposed change, and each will be a visible change to a test when it is fixed.

## The thinking behind it

None of this was built first and explained after. Each piece is an article on newsroom.sgit.ai, written before it shipped and again when it went live. For an editor or an executive, start with these four:

[The case
### The future of news is a story vault, not a paywall
Why the unit of news should be a story a reader can hold, not a wall they must cross.
]({{newsroom}}/articles/future-of-news-story-vault-not-paywall.html)
[The thesis
### Sell the graph
The newsroom's founding idea: the value is in the connections between what is published, and that is what a reader pays for.
]({{newsroom}}/thesis/)
[Economics
### Paying the fact creator
What a meter makes possible that a subscription does not: money that follows the reading, down to the person who found the fact.
]({{newsroom}}/economics/)
[Going live
### Going live with the reading meter
The day real money started moving, what was switched on, and the line between what runs and what is designed.
]({{newsroom}}/articles/going-live-with-the-reading-meter.html)

More: [the articles behind it](../articles/), in reading order. The design pages on [corrections that propagate, provenance as the product, and content rights]({{newsroom}}/design/) are the newsroom's own.

## Starting a pilot

If you run a newsroom and want to try this on a section of your site, with your own payment link and your own lane, the people behind newsroom.sgit.ai will help you set it up and will learn from what your readers do. Write to [agent@riskmandate.ai](mailto:agent@riskmandate.ai), which an agent reads first and a person answers, or open [an issue]({{github}}/issues) in the repository, which is where the work happens in any case. Share this page with your team: the [developer quick start](../for-developers/) is what they will ask for next, and [the evaluator's page](../for-evaluators/) is what your security team will.

# Add the meter to a page

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/how-to/add-the-meter/>

> Put the reading meter on your site: the element at the foot of each page, the balance chip in the nav, the JSON config written once by your build, the pinned import, the account pages, and the article feed the picks read.

# Add the meter to a page

> Ten lines on each page, one config written by your build, and five account pages you copy. Nothing to deploy but files.

## 1. The element, where the charge happens

At the foot of the content, after the last paragraph a reader would reach:

```html
<sg-meter view="page" kind="article" date="2026-10-11" topics="newsroom sg-meter"
          title="Going live with the reading meter"></sg-meter>
```

`kind` is the price class (`article`, `issue`, `note`, `collection`, `page`, `free`); an article newer than `newDays` is charged as `article_new`. `date` and `topics` feed the personas' picks; `title` is what the history shows. A page that should charge nothing is `kind="free" quiet`, which keeps the balance on screen without a card (a synthetic reader once took a vanished chip for lost credit).

## 2. The chip, in the navigation

```html
<sg-meter class="meter-nav" view="balance"></sg-meter>
```

On every page, so a reader never loses sight of their balance. It marks a negative balance and opens the account.

## 3. The config, once

A JSON block with id `sg-meter-config`, the same on every page; write it in your build so it cannot drift. Prices in pence; every key has a default. The full shape and a live example are on [the developer quick start](../../for-developers/). The parts you will change:

```json
{"start": 500, "newDays": 7, "symbol": "£",
 "prices": {"article_new": 10, "article": 5, "issue": 3, "note": 2, "collection": 2, "page": 1, "free": 0},
 "topup": {"amount": 500, "link": ""},
 "links": {"account": "account/index.html", "topup": "account/top-up.html", "how": "about/the-meter.html"},
 "picks": {"feed": "articles/graphs.json", "base": "articles/"},
 "share": {"contact": ".well-known/sgit-subscribe.json", "form": "reading-share", "site": "your-site.example", "max": 300}}
```

Leave `topup.link` empty until your Stripe Payment Link exists: the top-up page then says that no money moves. The newsroom's gate refuses a test-mode link on a live page.

## 4. The import

```html
<script>
import('https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/{{release}}/assets/components/sg-meter/v1/v1.4/v1.4.0/sg-meter.js')
 .catch(function (e) { console.error('[sg-meter] component failed to load:', e); });
</script>
```

Pinned to a release and a component version; neither is ever edited in place. Generate the URL from one place in your build ([taking a release](../take-a-release/)).

## 5. The account pages

Five pages your site serves, each a shell around one view: `account/index.html` (`view="account"`), `account/top-up.html` (`topup`), `account/topped-up.html` (`topped-up`; set it as the Stripe link's return URL with `?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}`), `account/newsroom.html` (`newsroom`), `account/personas.html` (`personas`), and `account/share.html` (`share`). Copy the newsroom's: [account/](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/account/). The paths go in `links` and `links2` of the config.

## 6. The feed

`articles/graphs.json` with one entry per article (`slug`, `title`, `date`, `url`, `teaser`, `topics`, `tags`) is what the picks and the persona graph read. The newsroom's build writes it from the articles; yours can write it from whatever you have. Without it the meter still charges; the newsroom view says the list could not be loaded.

## 7. Check it

Open a page: the chip shows £5.00; scroll to the foot and watch the balance fall; rate the page at the card and see the price move; reload in the same tab and see nothing charged twice. Then run `tests/test_meter.mjs` against your site ([running the tests](../run-the-tests/)).

## What to read before going live

[Going live with the reading meter](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/going-live-with-the-reading-meter.html) for what was switched on and in what order, [Who will game the reading meter](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/who-will-game-the-reading-meter.html) for the threat model, and [the security model](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/meter/security.html) for the gaps the design accepts.

# How-to guides

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/how-to/>

> One task each: add the meter to a page; make a reading-list link; open the newsroom as a persona; set up the subscribe lane; take a release and roll one back; run the tests; make a release.

# How-to guides

> One task each, in the order a site adopts the API. The newsroom's pages are the worked examples throughout; its repository is public.

- [**Add the meter to a page**](add-the-meter/): the element, the config, the import, the balance chip, the account pages, and the two data files your site publishes.
- [**Make a reading-list link**](reading-list-link/): by hand from the grammar, or with the make page; what the recipient sees.
- [**Open the newsroom as a persona**](persona-link/): persona pages and links, `persona/links.json`, what a visitor persona is.
- [**Set up the subscribe lane**](subscribe-lane/): a key pair, a vault on an SG/Send host, the contact file at `/.well-known/`, and reading the lane with the key alone.
- [**Take a release, roll one back**](take-a-release/): for a site that consumes the API; the newsroom's procedure as the example.
- [**Run the tests**](run-the-tests/): in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox, against the newsroom's pages or your own.
- [**Make a release**](make-a-release/): for maintainers: version, cut, check, pull request, deploy, the live check.
