# Make a release

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/how-to/make-a-release/>

> For maintainers: the rules while the files are frozen, the version file, cutting a release directory and its manifest, the checks, the pull request with a person and an agent reviewer, the deploy, the tag and the live check, then the consumers.

# Make a release

> A release is a directory that is never changed after it is on `dev`, the default branch. The tree is always exactly the release the version file names, or the check fails.

## The rules, while the files are frozen

Until phase 4 of [the brief](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/explorer-to-villager-newsroom.html) is finished (the refactoring with every test passing, and the adversarial exercise), the served files change only as a new release, each change with a test that fails without it and a reason in the pull request. A fix to a finding is a deliberate change to the test that pinned it. A new reader feature is built here, as a new versioned file, never in the newsroom's tree.

## 1. Change, and test

Edit under the served paths (`assets/`, `for/`, `wire/`, `passkey/`); if the file is one of the meter's, it is a new component version at a new path, never an edit of `v1.4.0`. Run the tests in the three engines against the newsroom checkout ([running the tests](../run-the-tests/)).

## 2. Version and cut

`tools/version.json` holds two numbers and a date, all from the file, never the clock:

- **`version`**, the repository's version. Every change that lands on `dev` is a new one, in small increments: a patch for a small change (v0.2.1, v0.2.2, ...), a minor for a new capability. The deploy tags it, and refuses a version that is already a tag or not above the latest. CI on a branch fails when the version is not above `dev`'s.
- **`release`**, the latest cut of the reader code: `releases/<release>/`, what the consuming sites pin. It changes only when a served file changes; then it is set to the new version and cut.

```sh
$EDITOR tools/version.json          # {"version": "v0.2.3", "release": "v0.2.3", "date": "2026-10-20"} for a change to a served file;
                                    # {"version": "v0.2.3", "release": "v0.2.0", ...} for a change to the site, the tests or the tools
python3 tools/release.py cut        # (served files changed) releases/v0.2.3/<every served file> and manifest.json
python3 tools/release.py check      # every release matches its manifest; the tree is the release; the two numbers obey their rule
python3 site/build.py               # the site: the version in the bar, the release on /releases/
python3 site/check.py               # the site's gate: references, canonical, chrome, sitemap, llms, no key shapes
```

Add the version's line to `site/data/versions.json` (newest first); the build refuses a version without one, and `/versions/` shows them all. A new page needs its link-preview card: `python3 site/og.py` draws one into `site/og/` for every page that has none (commit it; the gate fails a page without one).

`cut` refuses to write over an existing release directory, refuses a release that is not the repository's version, and refuses a file that differs from the newsroom's bytes unless `CHANGED_FROM_NEWSROOM` records why. Write a release's note at `site/releases/v0.2.3.md`.

## 3. The pull request

CI runs the syntax check, the manifest check, the build twice, the site check and the tests in three engines. A pull request needs one person and one agent reviewer; the agent's review is a required check. The description says what changed, which test fails without it, and why now.

## 4. Merge, deploy, tag, check

A push to `dev` (the default branch, and the release branch) runs `deploy-pages.yml`: the checks again, a tag of the version, the Pages deploy of `www/` and `releases/`, and then `tools/live_check.py`, which asks the live host for every file of the release and compares the hashes, retrying while Pages propagates. The release is live when that job is green, not before.

## 5. The consumers

Tell the newsroom (and sgit.ai, once it pins): [taking a release](../take-a-release/). The newsroom's release note names the API release it moved to.

## What never happens

A file under `releases/` is never edited. A tag is never moved. A release is never cut from a tree that differs from it. A served file is never loaded unversioned.



---

# Open the newsroom as a persona

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/how-to/persona-link/>

> Persona links, persona pages and links.json: how a link opens the site as a founder, a journalist, a security lead, a builder or a board member, what a visitor persona is, and how a site defines its presets.

# Open the newsroom as a persona

> A link that says who you are reading as. The reader can keep the persona or send it away; nothing is charged for arriving.

## The links

```
https://newsroom.sgit.ai/persona/founder/
https://newsroom.sgit.ai/persona/#journalist
```

Five starting personas: `founder` (Morgan), `journalist` (Rowan), `security` (Sam), `builder` (Kai), `board` (Jordan). [`persona/links.json`](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/persona/links.json) lists them with their pages, for whoever writes the email. The picker at [`/persona/`](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/persona/) shows all five; an unknown id is said so, and nothing is added.

## What happens

The page's meter is in its `landing` view. It adds the persona as a *visitor*: active, with its starting reading list and picks, but marked as arrived by a link. The page says who you are reading as and offers *Keep* (it becomes one of the reader's own) and *Remove* (it goes, and the others stay). Opening the link twice adds nothing twice. The article [A link to a persona](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/a-link-to-a-persona.html) is the design, with the vault as the step after it.

## Defining the presets

Each preset is an entry in the meter config's `personas.presets`: `id`, `label`, `name`, `theme` (a hex colour), `blurb`, `topics` (weights by topic) and `articles` (the starting list, by slug). A persona added to the config gets its page and its row in `links.json` on the next build. The newsroom's `admin/build/personas.py` writes `persona/index.html`, one page per preset, and `links.json`; its pages carry the meter block with `view="landing"` and the id in the address.

## What a persona does afterwards

It curates: *Keep* and *Not for this persona* on any reader card move an article onto or off its lists, and the picks on the newsroom page follow what it kept. A page read is credited to the active persona. A reading list opened from a link is a persona of this kind too, named for the list.



---

# Make a reading-list link

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/how-to/reading-list-link/>

> Send someone a set of articles as one link, by hand from the grammar or with the make page; what they see when they open it; how a site adds the two pages.

# Make a reading-list link

> A list is a link. Make it with the page, or type it.

## With the make page

Open [newsroom.sgit.ai/for/make.html](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/for/make.html). Search the articles, add up to fifty, move them up and down, mark some as *worth a look* rather than *to read*, name yourself and the reader, write a note, and copy the link. The preview shows the list exactly as the recipient will see it, because the page reads its own link back through the recipient's parser. Every article page also has a *start a reading list with it* link at its foot, which opens the make page with that article in it.

## By hand

```
https://newsroom.sgit.ai/for/#from=Dinis&to=Steve&r=78,42,15&s=66&n=Read%2078%20first
```

`r` is the articles to read, in order, by number; `s` is worth a look; `from` and `to` are names; `n` is a note. The numbers are in [`articles/ids.json`](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/ids.json), and each article prints its own (*Article No. 78*). The rules, field by field: [the reading-list link](../../docs/reading-list-link/).

## What the recipient sees

The list, with each article's title, date and teaser, in the order you gave; your note; a Reply button if you gave an address. Opening it adds a visitor persona named for the list, which they can keep or remove; nothing is charged for opening it. Anything malformed in the link is dropped and listed under *Left out*, so a mangled link still opens.

## For a site

Two pages that import from this host, and a numbers file:

1. Publish `articles/ids.json` with a stable `n` per article (never changed or reused).
2. `for/index.html`: `import { openList } from 'https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/{{release}}/for/reading-list.js'` and call `openList({ core, ids: '../articles/ids.json', root: '../', mount })` with `core` the meter core's URL on this host. Load `for/for.css` from this host too.
3. `for/make.html`: the same with `makeList` from `for/make.js` and `site: 'https://your-site/for/'`, the address the links will carry.

The newsroom's `admin/build/lists.py` writes both pages; copy it or the pages it writes.



---

# Run the tests

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/how-to/run-the-tests/>

> The eleven test files, what each covers, how the harness serves a newsroom checkout and routes this host to the working tree, the three engines, which tests need Chromium, and how to run them against your own pages.

# Run the tests

> No mocks of the code: real browsers, the real pages, a real vault library against a mock of the vault API, and the sgit command line. The harness swaps one thing only: requests to this host are answered from the working tree.

## Set up

```sh
git clone {{github}} && cd SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API
npm install --no-save --no-audit --no-fund playwright@1.56.1
npx playwright install --with-deps chromium        # and webkit, firefox, as you need
python3 -m pip install 'sgit-ai==0.21.0'           # the vault test's CLI round trip, the notes test's lane
git clone https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom .newsroom   # the pages the tests run against
```

`tests/newsroom.json` names the commit CI checks the newsroom out at. `NEWSROOM=<path>` points the tests at any checkout, including your own site once it imports the code.

## Run

```sh
node tests/test_meter.mjs                       # Chromium, the default
BROWSER=firefox node tests/test_lists.mjs
BROWSER=webkit  node tests/test_search.mjs
NEWSROOM=/path/to/your/site node tests/test_meter.mjs
```

A test prints `ok` or `FAIL` per check and exits 1 on any failure. It prints `SKIP` and exits 0 when it cannot run (no browser, no newsroom checkout, no `sgit`); CI treats a `SKIP` as a failure, so a missing install cannot pass quietly.

## What each file covers

| Test | Covers | Engines |
|---|---|---|
| `test_styles` | the served stylesheets write no colour outside a theme token (the newsroom's rule, held here since the files moved) | Node |
| `test_site` | this website: the five themes' tokens, no literal colour in its stylesheet, the picker and its memory, 4.5:1 in every theme, the bar at ten widths | all three |
| `test_meter` | the meter in a browser: depth, rating, decline, reload, below zero, the return page, personas, picks, export and restore, the share form, the persona links, phone width | all three |
| `test_lists` | the reading-list parser in Node and the two pages in a browser: malformed input, limits, the make page, copy, phone width | all three |
| `test_review` | the review's findings, pinned as the behaviour is today (R1 to R11, R14, R15, R17) | all three; R2 is held in Chromium |
| `test_wire` | the wire pages reading the real vault: edition, lenses, sources, documents, what left the browser | all three (needs the vault host) |
| `test_graphs` | the wire's graphs: the lenses' edges and the picture drawn from the real vault | all three (needs the vault host) |
| `test_sync` | the activity vault's logic as pure functions, two devices' states | all three (Node) |
| `test_search` | the index and the ranking in Node, the page in a browser | all three |
| `test_vault` | the vendored library against the mock, the newsroom's layer, the sgit CLI round trip | Node + CLI |
| `test_passkey` | the passkey lab with a virtual authenticator that has PRF | Chromium (CDP) |
| `test_pane` | the pane: the account carried between three devices through the mock | Chromium (CDP) |
| `test_notes` | the feedback loop end to end: notes, the lane, the CLI reading it, a second device | Chromium (CDP) |
| `test_inbox` | the pane's inbox and send: a link held, a QR code decoded, a second device | Chromium (CDP) |
| `test_ask` | ask: passages and messages in Node; the reader's key and the faked built-in model in a browser | Chromium |

Chromium's clipboard permissions have no equivalent in Firefox and WebKit, so the three clipboard reads run in Chromium only; the rest of each test runs everywhere.

## In CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the syntax check, the manifest check and the reproducible build, then the tests in a matrix of the three engines against the pinned newsroom commit, on every push and pull request; about four minutes. The brief's target is two; caching the engines is the first thing to measure.



---

# Set up the subscribe lane

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/how-to/subscribe-lane/>

> How shares, subscriptions and notes reach a newsroom without a server: a key pair, a write-only lane in an encrypted vault on an SG/Send host, the contact file at /.well-known/, and reading the lane with the key alone.

# Set up the subscribe lane

> A reader presses Send; their browser encrypts a small message to your public key and appends it to a lane you own. The site never sees it. You read the lane with your key, by hand or with an agent.

## What you need

1. **A key pair.** An RSA key whose public half is published; the private half stays with whoever (or whichever agent) reads the lane. The envelope is RSA-OAEP-SHA256 wrapping an AES-256-GCM key (the sgit hybrid envelope v2).
2. **A vault with an append lane** on an SG/Send host, with an append token that lets a browser write and nothing else. The newsroom's lane is on `dev.send.sgraph.ai` (named *dev*; finding R5 asks the operator to say whether that is production).
3. **The contact file** at `/.well-known/sgit-subscribe.json`.

## The contact file

```json
{"format": "sgit-subscribe/v1",
 "site": "your-site.example",
 "recipient": {"address": "newsroom@your-site.example", "fingerprint": "<sha256 of the PEM>", "encrypt": "<PEM public key>"},
 "inbox": {"vault": "<vault id>", "endpoint": "https://<sg-send host>", "encrypt_to": "recipient",
           "status": "live", "lane": {"name": "subscribe", "append_token": "<token that can only append>"}}}
```

The browser recomputes the fingerprint from the PEM before encrypting, so a swapped key is refused. The newsroom's own file is [here](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/.well-known/sgit-subscribe.json); it is still labelled with the site the code came from ([finding R4](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/4)), which the move makes possible to fix.

## What arrives

A subscription is an `.eml` with the address and a consent line; a share is the reader's summary and their data as JSON (balance, spent, reads, personas, topics, log; never a payment reference), with headers `X-SGit-Form`, `X-SGit-Reply-To`, `X-SGit-Name`, `X-SGit-Subscribe`, `X-SGit-Page`. A note from the vault pane arrives in the reader's own lane, whose read key they hand over, with the page, their words and the phrase they selected.

## Reading the lane

With `sgit` and the read key, from the command line or an agent:

```sh
sgit clone <the lane's read key>          # the notes as files, newest first
NEWSROOM_LANE_KEY=<read key> python3 admin/build/lane.py   # the newsroom's digest, by page; the key from the environment, never a file
```

A read key cannot write: a push from the clone is refused, and the test proves it. The newsroom refuses to hold a vault key for a reader's lane at all.

## The pieces on this host

`assets/subscribe.js` (the form, the fingerprint check, the envelope, the append), the meter's share view in `sg-meter.js`, and the vault layer for notes. The article [The site is an inbox](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/the-site-is-an-inbox.html) is the design of the feedback loop; [Two agents, one vault](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/two-agents-one-vault.html) is how the newsroom's agents share what arrives.



---

# Take a release, roll one back

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/how-to/take-a-release/>

> For a site that consumes the API: pin one release in one file, generate every URL from it, keep a copy of the manifest, check every page against it, and roll back by changing the line. The newsroom's procedure as the worked example.

# Take a release, roll one back

> One file names the release. Everything else is generated from it, and a gate refuses anything that is not.

## 1. Pin

Write the release in one place your build reads, and copy that release's manifest beside it. The newsroom's:

```json
{"host": "https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai", "release": "{{release}}"}
```

```sh
curl -s https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/{{release}}/manifest.json > admin/build/api-manifest.json
```

## 2. Generate every URL from the pin

Nothing in a page names a reader file by a relative path or by a release typed by hand. The newsroom's builders call `api_url(path)`; its sync points imported pages at the same URL; `python3 admin/build/api.py --repoint` rewrites every page in one pass when the pin changes, and `--rerecord` recomputes the content hashes its import gate keeps.

## 3. Gate it

Before a release of your site, check three things on every page: no reader file is loaded by a relative path; every reader file is loaded from the pinned release; every path loaded is in the manifest. The newsroom's `validate.js` check 14 does this; check 13 holds the frozen meter copies it still serves to the manifest's bytes. The checks are small because the rule is simple.

## 4. Verify the live host

After your deploy, ask this host for the hash of every file you load and compare with the manifest; `tools/live_check.py` in the repository does it for a release, with retries while Pages propagates. [Green does not mean live](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/green-does-not-mean-live.html).

## 5. Roll back

Change the release in the pin to the previous one, copy its manifest, repoint, gate, deploy. A release directory is never edited in place, so the previous release is exactly what it was.

## Taking a new release

Read [its notes](../../releases/) first: a release says what changed, and lists any file that differs from the newsroom's bytes and why. Then steps 1 to 4. The frozen meter versions are in every release at their paths, so a page pinned to an older component version keeps working.



---

# A newsroom's reader, as an API

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/>

> The reading meter, pay-after-you-read, personas, reading lists in a link, the reader's vault: the code a newsroom's reader runs, open source, served from one host, live on newsroom.sgit.ai and taking money.

# A newsroom's reader, as an API.

A reading meter that charges by how far you read. Paying after you read, with a rating that sets the price. Personas, a newsroom of your own, reading lists in a link, encrypted sharing, a vault that carries your account between devices. All of it runs in the reader's browser, with no server of ours, and all of it is open source. It is live on [newsroom.sgit.ai]({{newsroom}}/), and it is taking money.

[For publishers and editors](for-publishers/)[Quick start for developers](for-developers/)[For evaluators](for-evaluators/)

{{release}} · {{files}} files · {{reader_lines}} lines of reader code · {{tests}} checks in three browser engines · Apache 2.0

[Publishers, editors, executives
### What your readers get, what you keep, what it costs
A meter instead of a paywall, a reader's own newsroom instead of a feed, and a model where their data stays in their browser. The case, with the articles that made it and the numbers from a live site.
](for-publishers/)
[Developers
### Add the meter to a page in ten lines
Pinned, versioned files on one host; a JSON config; a custom element. The contracts your pages and agents program against, the data your site publishes, and the tests you can run against your own pages.
](for-developers/)
[Security, architecture, procurement
### Read the map, the review and the proof
Everything a reader can do, every place data leaves the browser, eighteen findings as public issues, a release manifest of hashes, and a move proved byte for byte.
](for-evaluators/)

## What is live today

{{live: [newsroom.sgit.ai]({{newsroom}}/) runs this release: {{articles}} articles behind a reading meter, with real payments through a Stripe link, personas, reading lists, the vault and the pane, search, and the Industry Wire read from a vault. It is the reference deployment and the first consumer of this API; [what runs and what is only designed]({{newsroom}}/shipped/) is kept honest on its own page.}}

[The meter
### Pay by depth, after you read
A page is charged by the deepest point reached; a rating at the foot sets the price from nothing to double. £5 of credit to start, in the reader's own browser.
]({{newsroom}}/articles/going-live-with-the-reading-meter.html)
[Personas
### A newsroom of your own
Read as a founder, a journalist, a security lead, a builder or a board member; keep and reject articles; picks follow. A link can open the newsroom as a persona.
]({{newsroom}}/persona/)
[Reading lists
### From me to you, in a link
Every article has a number; a list is a link with the numbers in it. No account, no server, nothing stored but the link.
]({{newsroom}}/for/make.html)
[The vault
### Your account, between devices
A passkey opens a door; the door holds the key to a master vault; the account travels encrypted, and the newsroom never holds a key.
]({{newsroom}}/vault/)

## How it works, in one picture

The pages on the newsroom's origin load the reader code from api.newsroom.sgit.ai; the reader's state stays on the page's origin

newsroom.sgit.ai (your site)
the pages, the articles, the data
<sg-meter view="page" kind="article">
localStorage · sgit.meter.v1 · the reader's state
articles/graphs.json · ids.json · .well-known/…
api.newsroom.sgit.ai (this host)
/{{release}}/ · pinned · never edited in place
assets/components/sg-meter/…/sg-meter.js
for/ · assets/vault-pane/ · assets/search/ · manifest.json
import()
Stripe (payment) · an encrypted vault (lane, wire)
only when the reader acts

The code is served from this host at a versioned path and never changed after it is published. The reader's state belongs to the page's origin, so it stays with the newsroom whichever host serves the script, and the newsroom never sees it. Nothing leaves the browser unless the reader pays, shares or subscribes, and each of those is a published contract. [The hosting model, in full](docs/hosting/).

## Open source, and why that is the point

The code is Apache 2.0, in [one repository]({{github}}), with its tests, its release manifests, its review findings as issues, and the brief it was built to. A publisher can pin a release today and run it on their own pages; a developer can read every line; an evaluator can check every hash against the live host. Nothing here needs permission.

The newsroom that runs it is the reference, not the product. The aim is other newsrooms adopting the same reader, so that a reading list or a persona made on one site means something on another, and so that the formats, the article number, the list link, the share, the envelope, outlive any one publisher. [How to adopt it](adopt/), and [who to talk to](about/).

# The contracts

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/docs/contracts/>

> The fourteen contracts other sites, pages and agents program against: the meter config, a charged page, persona links, the reading-list link, article numbers, the return page, the export, the share, the envelope, the contact file, the wire's vault, events, a component, the import's rules.

## The contracts

| Contract | Shape | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| The meter config | storageKey, start, newDays, symbol, prices{article_new,article,issue,note,collection,page,free}, depth, minDepth, topup{amount,link}, packs, links{account,topup,how}, rating{price[5],more[5]}, autoKeep, picks{feed,base}, links2{newsroom,personas,share}, share{contact,form,site,max}, personas{presets[],names{}}, root | `sg-meter-core.js DEFAULTS; written into every page by sgit.ai's build and re-pointed by the import` |
| A charged page | <sg-meter view="page" kind="article/issue/note/collection/page/free" date="…" topics="a b" title="…" [quiet]>: the price class comes from the page | `sgit.ai's build for imported pages; page.py (kind=free, quiet) for this site's` |
| A persona link | /persona/<id>/ and /persona/#<id>, id ∈ {founder, journalist, security, builder, board} | `personas.py, persona/links.json` |
| A reading list link | /for/#from=&to=&r=&s=&f=&n=&e=: names ≤ 40 chars of letters, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes; r,s article numbers, 1–50 in all; f persona ids or c:<collection>, ≤ 10; n ≤ 240 chars; e an address | `for/reading-list.js LIMITS, parse(), build()` |
| Article numbers | articles/ids.json: n and slug are the contract, assigned once in publication order, never changed or reused; every other field is display text | `admin/build/ids.py; validate.js check 12` |
| The return page | ?session_id=<ref>: credited once per distinct value, never verified | `_toppedUp(), credit()` |
| The export | the state as JSON; restore accepts any file with balance:number and log:array | `restore()` |
| The share | a text summary then the same data as JSON {v:1, site, at, balance, spent, declined, reads, topups, active, personas, topics, cols, log}, as an .eml with X-SGit-Form, X-SGit-Reply-To, X-SGit-Name, X-SGit-Subscribe, X-SGit-Page | `shareData(), _send()` |
| The envelope | sgit hybrid envelope v2: {v:2, w, i, c} (RSA-OAEP-SHA256 wrapped AES-256-GCM key, iv, ciphertext), base64, then base64 again as the lane payload | `envelope(), subscribe.js encrypt()` |
| The contact file | sgit-subscribe/v1: recipient{address, fingerprint, encrypt}, inbox{vault, endpoint, encrypt_to, status, lane{name, append_token}}; the fingerprint is recomputed from the PEM before use | `.well-known/sgit-subscribe.json` |
| The wires' vaults | u9i9jp0l (the Industry Wire), eitf274v (OWASP), v202bla5 (AWS), p6twygul (Portugal) on dev.send.sgraph.ai, read keys published; data/bundle.json {beats, stories, sources, personas, brief; wire, map, stack when present}, data/deliveries.json, data/releases.json (wire-releases/v1, one entry per publish), docs/*.md; story fields, changes and status shown as written; everything in a vault is public, for ever | `admin/build/wire-vault*.json; wire/how.html; each wire's agents own its content` |
| Events | sg:meter.changed · charged · rated · declined · toppedup · reset · restored · persona · shared; sg-meter:error | `sg-meter-core.js _emit(), sg-component.js failed()` |
| A component | static jsUrl, get resourceName(), onReady(); a .tpl and a .css beside the .js; published at an immutable versioned path | `sg-component.js` |
| The import's rules | the meter path rewrite (v1.3.1 → v1.4.1), the top-up link, ten text rules, the article number line, the moved banner cut, the foot of every issue; each stops the import when its anchor moves | `sync_newsroom.py items 9–15` |


---

# State, inputs and outputs

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/docs/state/>

> Where a reader's data lives (localStorage on the page's origin), everything that comes in, and every channel by which anything leaves the browser.

## State

- `v`: 3
- `created`: ISO time
- `balance · spent · declined`: pence, to 0.1p
- `reads`: pages opened
- `paused`: always false since v1.4.0
- `log[]`: ≤ 500 entries: id, at, path, title, kind, topics, price, depth, cost, persona, autoKept?, rating{useful,more,detail,at}?, declined{reason,at,refunded}?
- `topups[]`: ref (≤ 40 chars), at, credit, source: link | simulated
- `sessions[]`: every payment reference credited, unbounded
- `cart[]`: the simulated cart (unused with a live link)
- `active`: the active persona's id
- `personas[]`: id, preset, name, created, on[], off[], visitor?, list? (a reading list's key), theme?
- `shares[]`: ≤ 20: at, how, pages

## Inputs

- **Element attributes**: view · kind · date · topics · title · quiet · count · persona · compact (the page's own markup (trusted: it is this site's build); `sg-meter.js`)
- **The page's config**: <script type="application/json" id="sg-meter-config"> (this site's build, written once per page; every key has a default; `sg-meter-core.js _config()`)
- **The address: query**: ?session_id= on account/topped-up.html (whoever made the link; any value is credited once (accepted, documented); `_toppedUp()`)
- **The address: fragment**: #<persona id> on persona/; #from,to,r,s,f,n,e on for/ and for/make.html (whoever made the link; validated field by field, the rest dropped and listed; `_named(), reading-list.js parse()`)
- **The address: path**: location.pathname (the charge is keyed on it; the slug is taken from it; the share records it; `open(), _page(), _send()`)
- **Local storage**: sgit.meter.v1 (the state), sgit.meter.v1.seen (session: the charge per path) (this browser, written by the meter; also by the reader, who may edit it (accepted); `_read(), _seen()`)
- **A file**: Restore from an export… (whoever made the file; checked for balance:number and log:array only; `restore()`)
- **Forms**: the share form, the subscribe form, the make page (the reader; email checked by a loose pattern, names by a strict one; `_send(), subscribe.js, make.js`)
- **The wires' vaults**: data/bundle.json (with wire, map or stack when the vault has them), data/deliveries.json, data/releases.json, docs/*.md, decrypted in the browser; one vault per wire (whoever holds the vault's write key (the wire's agents); drawn as text, links only from http(s) values, markdown rendered by an escaping renderer; the vault's own HTML is not used; `wire/wire.js`)
- **Own-origin data**: articles/graphs.json · articles/ids.json · .well-known/sgit-subscribe.json · sg-meter.tpl · sg-meter.css (this site's build; the contact file's key is checked against its fingerprint; `feed(), openList(), _send()`)
- **postMessage**: replies from the dev.vault.sgraph.ai frames (origin-checked; drives a status line only; `vault-ui-embed.js`)

## Outputs

- **GET, own origin**: every page, script, style, image and JSON; whenever a page opens; seen by GitHub Pages, which sees the request as any host does
- **POST https://dev.send.sgraph.ai/api/vault/append/write/y9j3nc60**: {append_token, payload}: an .eml encrypted in the browser to the lane's public key; when the reader presses Send on the share page or Subscribe; seen by the vault host; it sees ciphertext, a size and a time
- **Navigation to https://buy.stripe.com/…**: the reader leaves for Stripe's page and returns to /account/topped-up.html?session_id=…; when the reader presses Top up / Pay; seen by Stripe (card, email, name, postcode)
- **GET https://dev.send.sgraph.ai/api/vault/read/u9i9jp0l/…**: the ciphertext of the wire's vault: its head pointer, commit, tree and the files the page needs, decrypted in the browser with the published read key; when a wire page opens, and when the reader asks for a new commit; the pointer at most every two minutes; seen by the vault server; it sees the request and nothing of the reader
- **iframe https://dev.vault.sgraph.ai/?embed=1**: two frames; the published read key is posted to them; on the study page only; seen by the vault UI host
- **mailto:**: Reply to <sender> on a reading list; the subscribe fallback; when pressed; the page sends nothing; seen by the reader's mail client
- **A download**: reading-account.json: the whole state, payment references included; Export as JSON; seen by the reader's disk
- **The clipboard**: a link, or the share text; Copy; seen by the reader's clipboard
- **postMessage to the parent window**: {type:'sg-app-ready'} with targetOrigin *; when a page is framed; seen by whoever framed it


---

# The map, and the review

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/review/>

> Everything a reader runs on newsroom.sgit.ai, mapped before the move and reviewed line by line: the numbers, the eighteen findings as issues, the accepted gaps.

## The findings

| Finding | Severity | Area | What | Pinned by | Proposed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [R1](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/1) | medium | the meter's logic | Declining a page as “not relevant” leaves it in the persona's reading list. open() auto-keeps an article on first open; decline() refunds the charge but does not undo the auto-keep, so the article stays under “Its reading list” and profile() adds +5 for it while the decline subtracts 2: a page the reader rejected pulls its topics up. | test_review.mjs R1 (passes while the article stays in the list) | decline() removes an autoKept entry from the active persona's on[]; a reader who added it by hand keeps it |
| [R2](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/2) | low | restore from a file | restore() checks that the file has a numeric balance and a log array and nothing else. A persona without on[] and off[] makes the personas and newsroom views throw and show nothing; a log entry's path is rendered as the history link's href as it is; a persona's theme is written into a style attribute as it is. The file is the reader's own, so the exposure is a file someone else sent them to restore. | test_review.mjs R2 (the blank personas page); the href and theme cases are described, not pinned | normalise on read: personas get arrays, paths must be same-origin paths, themes must be a hex colour; unknown fields dropped |
| [R3](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/3) | low | the return page | A malformed percent sequence in ?session_id= (for example %E0%A4%A) makes decodeURIComponent throw inside onReady, so the element fails with “did not load: URI malformed” instead of saying the reference is missing. | test_review.mjs R3 | try/catch around the decode; treat an undecodable id as no id |
| [R4](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/4) | medium | data correctness | A reading share or a subscription sent from this site is labelled sgit.ai: the imported config has share.site = "sgit.ai" (so the text begins “My reading on sgit.ai”), subscribe.js writes From: site@sgit.ai, and the contact file says site: sgit.ai. The agent that drains the lane can tell the two sites apart only by the Sent from line. | test_review.mjs R4 | a recorded meter rule for share.site (admin/build/newsroom-meter.json); subscribe.js and the contact file are verbatim imports and need this site's own copies, or a parameter, after the move |
| [R5](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/5) | note | operations | On the live site the lane for shares and subscriptions is on dev.send.sgraph.ai and the study page's vault frames come from dev.vault.sgraph.ai. Both hosts are named “dev”. Production reader data goes to them. | test_review.mjs R5 (records the hosts) | a decision, not a code change: either these are the production hosts and say so, or the files point at production ones |
| [R6](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/6) | low | display | Money is kept to a tenth of a penny and shown to a penny. Balance and spent are each formatted on their own, so a half-penny state shows, from £5.00, a balance of £4.95 and £0.06 spent, which do not add up; the history shows 5.5p. A reader who checks the arithmetic finds a penny missing. | test_review.mjs R6 | one rounding rule for the pair (format spent as start − balance, or keep both to 0.1p on the account page) |
| [R7](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/7) | question | picks | picks() excludes every page in the log, whichever persona read it, while profile() is per persona. An article read as Morgan is never picked for Rowan. | test_review.mjs R7 (records the behaviour) | decide: per-persona exclusion, or keep and say so on the newsroom page |
| [R8](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/8) | low | robustness | feed() caches a failed fetch as null for the life of the page, so one transient failure leaves “The list of articles could not be loaded” on every view until a reload. | test_review.mjs R8 | do not cache a failure; retry on the next call |
| [R9](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/9) | medium | the number contract | If sgit.ai renames an article (a new slug), ids.py marks the old number withdrawn and gives the article a new number. A reading list that named the old number then says the article is no longer published, although it is. | described; a rename has not happened yet | a renamed_to field on the old entry, followed by the list page; the gate requires it when a slug disappears and a new one appears in the same import |
| [R10](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/10) | high for the move | Content-Security-Policy | Every imported page loads assets/site.js, subscribe.js and shots.js by fetching the text and running it with (0, eval)(text) (the loader's bridge path), and the loader and the meter config are inline. A script-src policy without 'unsafe-eval' and without hashes breaks every page. frame-ancestors cannot be set in a meta tag at all, and GitHub Pages sets no headers, so framing (the Keep, Remove and Top up buttons under another site) is not prevented today. | test_review.mjs R10 (counts the pages that eval) | load scripts with <script src> or import(); then a meta CSP for script-src and connect-src; frame-ancestors needs a host that sets headers |
| [R11](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/11) | high per the brief | the pipeline | The one workflow ran validate.js only; the browser tests (46 + 65 checks) never ran in CI. | fixed in this release: a reader-tests job runs all three test files before the tag | done; the move's pipeline adds WebKit and Firefox and a pre-production copy |
| [R12](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/12) | note for the move | two upstreams | The account pages, subscribe, the contact file and the component base are imported from sgit.ai on every sync and cannot be changed here except by a recorded rule, and verbatim files (scripts, JSON) cannot be changed by rule at all. R4 is the first consequence. The newsroom's meter is v1.4.0 while sgit.ai's is v1.3.1. | the brief's phase 1 removes it | the move: both sites pin released files |
| [R13](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/13) | note | what leaves | The export includes the payment references (sessions, topups[].ref) that the share deliberately leaves out. A reader who sends their export instead of their share sends them. | described | say so beside the button, or export without sessions |
| [R14](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/14) | low | bounds | sessions[] and topups[] grow without bound, and a payment reference is not checked for shape before it is stored. | described | cap both; keep references that look like cs_… only |
| [R15](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/15) | low | personas | persona(id) falls back to personas[0], which is “me” only when “me” is first; after a restore that puts another persona first, an unknown id resolves to that persona. | described | fall back to the persona with id me |
| [R16](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/16) | process | caching | Imported pages load the meter as sg-meter.js?v=<sgit.ai's release>, so the cache-buster never changes for a release of this site. That is fine while a published version is never edited in place, which is the rule; it is written here because v1.4.0 was edited in place while it was being built. | described | a change is a new version path, always |
| [R17](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/17) | note | reading lists | A list's persona is keyed by a 32-bit hash of the names and numbers, so two different lists can share one persona with probability about one in four billion per pair. | described | a longer hash, or the fragment itself as the key |
| [R18](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__API/issues/18) | note | listeners | The landing view adds a window hashchange listener per element and never removes it, and re-renders on every meter change (the picker's “Copied” label resets). | described | one listener, removed on disconnect |

# Versions

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/versions/>

> Every version of this repository that landed on dev, newest first, with the reader-code release each one serves and what changed, in a line.

- **v0.2.10** (2026-10-15, reader code v0.2.5): feed.xml: versions and releases as RSS, linked from every page's head and from llms.txt; the gate checks it is well formed and current.
- **v0.2.9** (2026-10-15, reader code v0.2.5): The footer takes the newsroom's shape: who makes this and under whose responsibility, the network line, the participant disclosure, the version line with the reader-code release; the gate checks each.
- **v0.2.8** (2026-10-15, reader code v0.2.5): A link-preview card for every page (og:image 1200x630 and the Twitter card), drawn by site/og.py in Newsprint's colours and committed; the gate fails a page without one.
- **v0.2.7** (2026-10-15, reader code v0.2.5): The backfill's grep named two matchers at once and would have matched nothing; one matcher.
- **v0.2.6** (2026-10-15, reader code v0.2.5): The deploy tags every version in the history that has none (each commit's subject carries its version), so several versions landing in one push each get their tag.
- **v0.2.5** (2026-10-15, reader code v0.2.5): Reader-code release: wire/wire.css wraps a story's long words (a URL as plain text in the lead story's corrections overflowed a phone; test_wire caught it). The first change to a served file since the move, recorded in the manifest with its reason.
- **v0.2.4** (2026-10-14, reader code v0.2.0): The website's gate (site/check.py): every reference resolves, canonical and chrome on every page, the sitemap and llms files agree with the tree, a key-leak tripwire. The map and the proof data are published on the host. This versions page.
- **v0.2.3** (2026-10-14, reader code v0.2.0): test_review pins R2 as the personas page being unusable in either form (blank, or the element failed), as CI run 13 saw.
- **v0.2.2** (2026-10-14, reader code v0.2.0): The website wears the newsroom's five themes: its token file and bootstrap, unchanged; the picker in the bar; one row from 1280 up; print and reduced motion; tests/test_site.mjs as the gate.
- **v0.2.1** (2026-10-14, reader code v0.2.0): Every change that lands on dev is a version: tools/version.json holds the repository's version beside the reader-code release; the deploy tags the version and refuses a missed bump.
- **v0.2.0** (2026-10-14, reader code v0.2.0): The second cut of the reader code, from the newsroom at v0.12.50 (74 files; SG Meter v1.4.1, the inbox, the graphs, the QR library); the release the newsroom pins at its v0.13.0. The tests re-adapted, test_graphs and test_inbox added.
- **v0.1.0** (2026-10-13, reader code v0.1.0): The first cut of the reader code, from the newsroom at v0.12.10 (63 files), the pipeline, the proof of the move, and the website for publishers, developers, evaluators and agents.

# The articles behind it

<https://api.newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/>

> The newsroom.sgit.ai articles that designed, built and reviewed this API, curated for publishers, for the reader's own newsroom, and for the engineering.

## The case

- [The future of news is the story vault, not the paywall](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/future-of-news-story-vault-not-paywall.html) (2026-09-22, No. 11): Why a newsroom would want this at all.
- [A meter in the browser: a penny a page, a history you keep, and a site that picks for you](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/a-meter-in-the-browser.html) (2026-10-10, No. 57): The reading meter, as it was built.
- [Pay after you read: how a reading meter became a working business model in one afternoon, one release at a time](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/pay-after-you-read.html) (2026-10-10, No. 65): Paying after you read, with a rating that sets the price.
- [Going live with the reading meter: pay for what you read, go below zero if you like, and the numbers we will check in eight weeks](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/going-live-with-the-reading-meter.html) (2026-10-10, No. 60): Real money, and the line between what runs and what is designed.
- [Who will game the reading meter? Eight kinds of reader, nine ways to cheat, and the risks that will actually happen](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/who-will-game-the-reading-meter.html) (2026-10-10, No. 61): The threat model, written before the first pound.
- [No server, by design: first I retired the database, now I am retiring the back end](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/no-server-by-design.html) (2026-10-11, No. 72): Why there is no server of ours, and what that buys a reader.
## The reader's own newsroom

- [A link to a persona: send people to the newsroom as someone, not as nobody](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/a-link-to-a-persona.html) (2026-10-10, No. 66): A link that opens the newsroom as a persona.
- [Pay to keep your persona: readers should pay because it helps them, not because they feel they should](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/pay-to-keep-your-persona.html) (2026-10-10, No. 62): What a persona is worth, and to whom.
- [From me to you, in a link: a personal reading list, two briefs to build and use it, and the loop that makes it a day's work](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/a-reading-list-in-a-link.html) (2026-10-11, No. 74): From me to you, in a link: the reading-list grammar.
- [I miss it, so it is working: the people who decide the roadmap have to use the product, and the vault the newsroom now needs](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/i-miss-it.html) (2026-10-11, No. 76): The makers must use it, and the brief for the reader's vault.
- [The vault is live: from a design on 11 October to a reader's vault on newsroom.sgit.ai by two in the morning, and how all of it fits together](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/the-vault-is-live.html) (2026-10-12, No. 81): The reading account carried between devices.
- [The site is an inbox: deciding before reading, marks that build the reader's own graph, and why I could not write this brief until the vault existed](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/the-site-is-an-inbox.html) (2026-10-12, No. 82): Notes to the newsroom, carried by the vault.
- [The passkey opens the vault: a door per path, a master vault for every user, and no server of ours](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/the-passkey-opens-the-vault.html) (2026-10-11, No. 77): A passkey's PRF bytes compute a door; no server of ours.
- [Where the vault keys live: key management at sgit-ai v0.20.0, and what comes next](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/where-the-vault-keys-live.html) (2026-10-10, No. 64): Where the keys live, and who holds what.
## How it is engineered

- [Go slow to go fast: moving the newsroom from an explorer project to a villager one, with the brief to do it](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/explorer-to-villager-newsroom.html) (2026-10-11, No. 78): The brief for the move this repository is: go slow to go fast.
- [Code review as a fractal semantic graph: source code is already one, and the review should read every layer of it](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/code-review-as-a-fractal-semantic-graph.html) (2026-10-03, No. 23): The review method: read a change at every layer.
- [If somebody built a company on code review: how I would do it, and why it is only now possible](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/if-somebody-built-a-company-on-code-review.html) (2026-10-05, No. 27): Why villager code is read line by line.
- [Green does not mean live](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/green-does-not-mean-live.html) (2026-08-17, No. 1): A release ends by asking the live site for its version.
- [How to run synthetic users on your own site: five people who do not exist, a browser, and an afternoon](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/how-to-run-synthetic-users.html) (2026-10-10, No. 67): Five readers who do not exist, a browser, and an afternoon.
- [Brief the agent too: the people I talk to work with agents, so what I send has to reach both](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/brief-the-agent-too.html) (2026-10-11, No. 75): The people you talk to work with agents; brief their agents too.
- [Two agents, one vault: the Industry Wire is written into an encrypted vault by one agent and drawn by newsroom.sgit.ai, which holds only the read key](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/two-agents-one-vault.html) (2026-10-12, No. 80): Two agents, one vault: how the newsroom's agents share state.
